What happens when your vector database only sees isolated chunks? PaperQA fixes retrieval with a 88% boost.
How did researchers use PaperQA to achieve a 88% leap in retrieval accuracy?
Does PaperQA actually outperform standard vector retrieval by 88%, or is it just hype?
Why does standard vector search break down when summarizing an entire corpus? Enter PaperQA.

Everyone thought standard methods were enough, until PaperQA proved: retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) models have been proposed to reduce hallucinations and provide provenance for how an answer was generated.

Why is PaperQA a major breakthrough? Because large Language Models (LLMs) generalize well across language tasks, but suffer from hallucinations and uninterpretability, making it difficult to assess their accuracy without ground-truth.
Did you know lLMs hallucinate science because they treat peer-reviewed papers like generic training data, losing critical semantic provenance entirely?
